title: Prime Subtraction Operation
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, you can repeatedly subtract a prime number less than the current element's value from that element.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, you can repeatedly subtract a prime number less than the current element's value from that element. Determine if this operation can transform nums into a strictly increasing array. Return true if possible, otherwise return false.
constraints: For each index at most once, you may subtract a prime strictly smaller than its value.
Determine whether the resulting array can be strictly increasing.
Return True when possible and False otherwise.
hints: Process left to right and make each value as small as possible while remaining above the previous result.
Precompute primality up to the largest input value.
For each value, subtract the largest prime that still leaves a result greater than previous.
The greedy choice leaves maximum room for every later element; if even the unchanged value is too small, no solution exists.
editorial: The greedy choice leaves maximum room for every later element; if even the unchanged value is too small, no solution exists.

tests.explanation: Subtracting three and seven from the first two values yields [1, 2, 6, 10].
The final value three leaves too little room for both earlier positions.
